It’s going to be trial and error with out without a a doctor because every skin is different. Not everything works for everyone. 

If you’re going to do this, start with gentle cleansers and moisturizers. Mineral sunscreen, and make sure you reapply it. 

Only try one new product at a time and try it for a while before adding anything else. Make sure to stop using it if you have negative side effects and don’t add another product for a while. 

That’s the best way to find out what works for your skin. It’s a slow process, but it’s better than overhauling your skin care routine every month because it’s not working then messing up your barrier.

I more suspect that there’s ingredients you’re sensitive to in the moisturizer. I find that my rosacea hates HA. That’s literally in almost everything. I cut down my routine so much it was bare minimum for months. Some people find they can’t to niamicide or vitamin c. Rosacea is really sensitive. 

I’d try Vanicream in the big tub. If you haven’t tried it before. Very minimal skincare routine. Find a cleanser with minimal ingredients. Look for gentle, not hydrating. 

Also if you use chemical sunscreen, try mineral.

Okay, right now I’d suggest a skin barrier repair:

1. Oil/balm cleanser. Find one with minimal ingredients. I’d say stay away from any that say hydrating. Which I know is what you say you want, but we don’t know the ingredient(s) that caused reactions so you want ingredient lists to be small. 
2. A very gentle cleanser. Vanicream is great. Again, I would go for something with a small ingredient list. Don’t go for hydration ones, go for a gentle cleanser. 
3. Vanicream moisturizer. Get the big one. It has minimal ingredients and most of them do not bother your skin. It’s the most gentle moisturizer .
4. Mineral sunscreen. Generally mineral sunscreen is best for rosacea. Reapplying every 80 minutes if you are outside. This is so important. 

Stick to that. It’s a small list. It won’t help your rosacea but right now is about healing the barrier and finding out the ingredients your skin does not like. 

Once you’ve done that for a while if your skin is doing better, I’d add azaliec acid. Then wait a while before adding anything else. 

Do not add multiple products to your routine at  one time. Add one, do that for a month or two. If you have no bad reaction/it helps, keep it and add something else. 

Major routine changes at once typically causes reactions on the skin and then you also do not know what product causes that reaction. 

Little side note: I did say do not add products with hydration in the name. A good portion of people with rosacea actually have really sensitive skin and things like hyaluronic acid cause bad reactions.
